items.performers: Susan Gritton, soprano; Polyphony; The Choir of Trinity College, Cambridge; Britten Sinfonia; Stephen Layton, conductor
items.recorded: April 2007, All Hallows, Gospel Oak, London
items.label: Hyperion
items.note: Poulenc had Benedictine monks playing football in mind when he wrote the second movement of the Gloria. Layton’s choirs sing its rhythms precisely, and Susan Gritton sings the soprano solo.

items.performers: Catherine Dubosc (Blanche), Rita Gorr (the old Prioress), Rachel Yakar (the new Prioress), Martine Dupuy (Mère Marie), Brigitte Fournier (Constance), José van Dam (the Marquis de la Force), Jean-Luc Viala (the Chevalier de la Force), Michel Sénéchal (the Chaplain); Chorus and Orchestra of the Opéra National de Lyon; Kent Nagano, conductor
items.label: Virgin Classics (now Erato / Warner Classics)
items.note: Blanche, a frightened young aristocrat, joins a Carmelite convent during the French Revolution; in the last scene the sisters sing the Salve Regina and are guillotined one by one. Nagano’s Lyon recording won the 1993 Gramophone opera award. Rita Gorr, who sang Mère Marie in Dervaux’s Paris recording, sings the dying old Prioress here.

items.work: Sextet for piano, flute, oboe, clarinet, bassoon and horn, FP 100
items.performers: Philippa Davies, flute; Gareth Hulse, oboe; Richard Hosford, clarinet; Ursula Leveaux, bassoon; Richard Watkins, horn; Ian Brown, piano (The Nash Ensemble)
items.label: Hyperion
items.note: A theme first heard on the winds returns in all three movements of this sextet for piano and five wind instruments. Ian Brown and the Nash players perform it.
